answer: The gale multiplier is published, charged in karst, and nectar lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 4206 identities would post 3593 proofs and burn roughly 77 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
